page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-32 is a general-purpose server instance built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 32 vCPUs mapped to 16 physical Intel cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The instance is equipped with 128 GB of dedicated system memory, yielding a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong capabilities in memory bandwidth and multi-core execution. The instance achieves a strong rating in large-block uncached memory read and write operations, alongside a strong Geekbench multi-core score of 16013.0. Static web serving throughput is also strong at 44.06 GB/sec. However, single-core execution, database operations, and standard compression tasks fall within the average range. For advanced workloads, the Intel processor supports Advanced Matrix Extensions and AVX-512 vector instructions, which assist in localized AI tasks.

While the instance demonstrates strong performance in text generation for small LLM models, it exhibits poor performance for large-scale LLM text generation, dropping to 2.31 tokens/sec for 70B models due to the lack of dedicated GPU accelerators. Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and strong multi-threaded capabilities, the n4-standard-32 is optimized for general-purpose workloads, multi-threaded software compilation, image processing, and high-throughput static web serving.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-32 is a general-purpose server instance powered by an Intel x86_64 processor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores, 128 GB of system memory, and no local storage or GPU accelerators. The instance delivers strong performance in large-block memory bandwidth, multi-core processing, and static web serving throughput. It also supports advanced instruction sets like Intel AMX and AVX-512, which enhance localized vector and matrix computations. While it handles small-scale language model text generation efficiently, it is poorly suited for large-scale LLM inference due to the absence of dedicated hardware acceleration. This instance is optimized for multi-threaded software compilation, image processing, and high-throughput web serving.
